title: Rental inspections in Australia: attendance and scam checks

## **Australian Rental Questions Answered: Do You Have to Attend Inspections Yourself? Are Listings Genuine? How Can You Avoid Scams?**

Publication date: 2025-10-25

Estimated reading time: 7 minutes

Author: Qrent Team

### **I. Must You Attend an Inspection Yourself? Can Someone Attend on Your Behalf?**

The Australian rental process emphasises “transparency and confirmation”. Most legitimate agencies require **the tenant or an authorised representative to attend the inspection in person**, to make sure the tenant understands the property's actual condition.

For **international students who have not yet arrived in Australia**, there are three ways to complete an inspection:

- **Ask a Friend or Classmate to Attend on Your Behalf (Authorized Proxy Viewing)**

You can ask a local friend to attend in person and explain to the agent by email in advance: “I would like to send a representative to attend the inspection on my behalf.”

Agents will usually agree, but may ask for your friend's name and contact number.

- **Arrange an Inspection Through Qrent Partners**

If you are in China and cannot attend an inspection yourself, you can contact Qrent (through the official website or Xiaohongshu account) for help with a representative inspection. Staff will help verify the listing, record a video, note key property conditions and provide a report.

- **A Video Inspection Provided by the Agent (Virtual Inspection)**

Some large agencies (such as Ray White and LJ Hooker) upload short videos or virtual tours, which can help you gain an initial understanding of the property.

📍Suggestion: Inspecting the property yourself is the most reliable approach. If you choose a representative inspection, make sure the entire process takes place through the agency's official communication channels, and retain email records or video files.

### **II. What Does open inspection Mean? How Do You Book One?**

**Open inspection (an open viewing)** is the most common stage in Australian renting. It means the agent opens the property during a fixed period for prospective tenants to view it together.

A listing page often says:

“Open for inspection: Saturday 10:30am – 10:45am”

This means the property will be open for viewing on Saturday morning between 10:30 and 10:45.

**How to book:**

Click “Book Inspection” or “Register for Inspection” on the Realestate or Domain listing page;

Enter your name, email address and mobile number;

After submitting, you will receive a confirmation email or SMS reminder from the agent.

If you are overseas, you can add a note:

“I’m currently overseas and would like to request a video inspection.”

💡Tip: Properties in popular areas of Sydney and Melbourne (such as Kensington and Carlton) usually have very short inspection periods, so arriving 5–10 minutes early is recommended.

### **III. Is the Listing Information Genuine?**

On mainstream Australian platforms (such as Realestate and Domain), **the vast majority of listings genuinely exist**, because these platforms only allow registered agencies to publish information, and those agencies must hold a state government licence.

However, you should still be alert to some high-risk sources, for example:

“Private rentals” on Facebook Marketplace or Gumtree;

Unofficial listings circulated through social channels such as WeChat and QQ groups;

Advertisements with rents far below market rates and urgent requests for money transfers.

Tips for assessing whether a listing is genuine:

**Verify the Agency Name**—A legitimate agency displays its company name on the listing page (such as LJ Hooker Randwick).

**Compare Information Across Multiple Platforms**—If a property appears only on social media, it is very likely to be unsafe.

**Beware of Low-Price Traps**—A listing in central Sydney priced below 350AUD/week is most likely not genuine.

**Refuse Transfers to Personal Accounts**—Agencies usually require the Bond to be paid through a company account or a property trust account.

### **IV. How Can You Avoid Scams?**

**Do Not Send Money in Advance**

All fees (including the Bond and Holding Deposit) should be paid only after signing a formal rental agreement.

**Ask for a Formal Contract and Receipts**

Australia's standard contract is called a “Residential Tenancy Agreement”, and is managed uniformly through an agency or state government template.

**Verify the Agent's Credentials**

In New South Wales (NSW), you can check through the NSW Fair Trading website;

In Victoria (VIC), you can visit Consumer Affairs Victoria.

**Keep All Communication Records**

These include emails, text messages, inspection registration forms and transfer receipts.

**Trust Official Channels**

Give priority to verified platforms such as Realestate, Domain and Qrent, and avoid transactions through private messages.

### **V. Qrent's Suggestions**

**Understand Market Conditions in Advance**: Average rents in central Sydney are 450–550AUD/week, and competition for properties around schools is intense.

**Plan 2 Months Ahead**: If you have not yet arrived in Australia, you can first use the Qrent platform to understand average market rents and shortlist property types, then sign a lease in person after arriving.

**Budget Sensibly**: In addition to rent, each person needs to pay an average of about 30AUD/week for water, electricity and Internet (Bills). If the property is unfurnished, the initial furniture outlay is around 2000AUD.

Qrent is committed to providing international students with more genuine, transparent rental information that allows price comparisons, helping everyone understand the market clearly before arriving in Australia and avoid scams or information gaps.
